Best ragey in Tomohon!

Smoky, savory, tender. Marinated overnight and charred over real charcoal, served with steaming rice, garlicky kangkung, and a homemade sambal that’s got just the right kick. The portion’s huge, the flavor’s deep, and you’ll be dreaming about it later.

The place aint fancy, plastic stools, open grill, local chatter, but that’s the point. You’re here for honest, bold, unforgettable food, not decor.

Price? Not the cheapest, but every bite screams worth it. You’re not paying for plating or ambiance. You’re paying for flavor that sticks with you.

If you’re in Tomohon and skip this? You messed up.

5-stars. No notes. Just go.

The area is huge! Plenty of space to walk around and enjoy the view.

Definitely worth the visit.

Unfortunately, this was the worst accommodation experience of our entire Indonesia trip.

The hotel is clearly very old (around 30 years) and unfortunately it shows everywhere. We raised our concerns during our stay but not received any response or reaction, which was very disappointing.

When we arrived, we were the only guests and the whole property felt completely deserted. There was no welcome drink and, most importantly, the restaurant was closed, even though this place is widely advertised and known for it. This was not communicated to us at all, despite being in direct contact before our arrival.

In our room, we found dead animals that attracted ants. We understand being close to nature, but this is absolutely not acceptable for a hotel charging 1,500,000 IDR per night. We have stayed in hotels in Indonesia that were three times nicer for a quarter of the price.

The only positive aspect is that the place can be recommended for breakfast or lunch only, as the view is beautiful and the staff are friendly and kind.

However, the owner should seriously reconsider charging such a high price, as the value offered is nowhere near what is advertised.

Very disappointing overall.

I ordered nasi kuning, portion size quite big, with generous topping : cakalang (skipjack) floss, vermicelli, crispy taro floss (not sure what abon bete means in English).
They use a bit drier rice compared to other nasi kuning sellers in Bitung. It wasn't clumpy.
My side order was tahu isi (fried tofu stuffed with vegetables, battered). It tastes fresh.
When asked whether the food is halal or not, they said they only use fish (and chicken egg) as source of animal protein. I trust them.
Overall: food is good. But the dining floor needs better lighting and air circulation. Trust me, it's hot.
One portion of nasi kuning and 2 tahu isi costs me Rp. 16,000.
Parking: space available for motorbikes at the front side, and road side parking for cars.

If you're a  coffee nerd, you should go here. The owner is extremely knowledgeable about coffee, and they produce superb specialty coffee. Now, people often rave about "good coffee", and this means different things to different people, so let me explain more.

I'm a big fan of specialty coffee. By "specialty", I mean coffee that has a cupping score of 80+ from the Specialty Coffee Association - generally light roasts with interesting flavours. For context, I like to make my coffee with a Hario V60.

I ordered 4 cups of coffee, all locally grown and produced: 1 fully washed, 1 natural, 1 honey process, and one anerobic fermentation. They were all excellent. The natural process coffee was light and fruity and didn't have any of the grassy flavour that some naturals do.

The star of the show was the anerobic fermentation coffee. I've drank a lot of specialty coffee, including doing may tastings directly from the farm in Colombia, Panama, Costa Rica etc., but I've never tasted a coffee like this one. It tasted like chocolate cake (literally) with a very strong vanilla flavour and perhaps some hazelnut notes, and it was not bitter at all. And it didn't have any of that funky flavour that sometimes comes with anerobic fermentation; I would not have been able to tell it was processed this way by its taste. The flavours were so strong and clean, I would have thought  it had vanilla syrup added (it did not!); I did not know coffee could taste like this.

Additionally, everything was crafted with care. Different coffees were provided in different cups, paired with them to best show off their flavours. The anerobic fermented coffee came in a pottery mug that was handmade in Japan.

Finally, the owner was extremely knowledgeable and passionate about coffee. I chatted with him for a couple of hours and learned a lot about the local varieties and his processing methods. He also showed me his small lab farm out back, where he tests out growing different varieties and natural methods of pest-protection and soil enrichment.

If you're a specialty coffee lover, and you're in Tomohon, you absolutely need to come here.
Elmont is such a lovely guy and the coffee is absolutely delicious. I also learned a lot about the production and coffee making, he even showed us the plants behind the house.

Can I give them 10 stars? Visiting a coffee plantation was at the top of my Tomohon bucket list, so we were ecstatic when we stopped into this coffee shop and they offered to give us a tour of their plantation and cultivation process. The coffee was phenomenal and we loved trying coffee grown on the slopes of Tomohon’s own Mount Mahawu. It was a neat experience to learn about the process and know exactly where the coffee we drank came from. We highly recommend having a pourover with their house blend which features their very own robusta and arabica beans. I also loved their kopi susu! The owners are beautiful, kind people. We highly recommend visiting them!

I admit the coffee here is delicious, but personally, the owner was very nice at first, but after a long time as a customer, there were several things that felt uncomfortable, such as being too crazy about someone's personal matters, which is not a problem once or twice, but if it happens repeatedly, it makes me want to look for another shop even though the quality is slightly lower.
